The **Women's Team Archery** event at the **2012 Summer Olympics** in London was held at **Lord's Cricket Ground** from **27 to 29 July 2012**. Here’s a detailed breakdown of the competition:

---

### **Key Details**
- **Venue:** Lord’s Cricket Ground, London
- **Date:** 27–29 July 2012
- **Format:**
  - **Ranking Round:** Each team (3 archers) shot 72 arrows (24 per archer) to determine seeding.
  - **Elimination Rounds:** Single-elimination matches (best-of-24 arrows, 8 per archer).
  - **Finals:** Gold and bronze medal matches.
- **Distance:** 70 meters (standard Olympic distance)
- **Equipment:** Recurve bows (no compound bows in Olympic archery)

---

### **Participating Teams & Results**
A total of **12 teams** (36 archers) competed, with the top 4 teams receiving a bye to the quarterfinals.

#### **Ranking Round (27 July)**
Teams were seeded based on the sum of their archers' individual ranking scores.

| **Rank** | **Team**          | **Total Score** | **Individual Scores** (A+A+A) |
|----------|-------------------|-----------------|-------------------------------|
| 1        | **South Korea**   | 1993            | Lee Sung-jin (671), Ki Bo-bae (668), Choi Hyeon-ju (654) |
| 2        | **United States** | 1979            | Miranda Leek (656), Khatuna Lorig (669), Jennifer Nichols (654) |
| 3        | **China**         | 1946            | Cheng Ming (647), Fang Yuting (652), Xu Jing (647) |
| 4        | **Japan**         | 1931            | Kaori Kawanaka (659), Ren Hayakawa (637), Miki Kanie (635) |
| 5        | **Chinese Taipei**| 1929            | Lin Chia-en (653), Tan Ya-ting (640), Le Chien-ying (636) |
| 6        | **Russia**        | 1927            | Ksenia Perova (659), Kristina Timofeeva (634), Inna Stepanova (634) |
| 7        | **Mexico**        | 1922            | Aída Román (658), Natalia Sánchez (636), Mariana Avitia (628) |
| 8        | **Great Britain** | 1901            | Naomi Folkard (640), Amy Oliver (634), Alison Williamson (627) |
| 9        | **Italy**         | 1890            | Pia Carmen Lionetti (640), Jessica tomada (625), Natalia Valeeva (625) |
| 10       | **Ukraine**       | 1868            | Lidiia Sichenikova (645), Tetyana Dorokhova (612), Margarita Shidler (611) |
| 11       | **Denmark**       | 1865            | Louise Laursen (635), Maja Jager (616), Anne Marie Laursen (614) |
| 12       | **India**         | 1854            | Deepika Kumari (648), Laishram Bombayla Devi (619), Cheswala Krishna (587) |

---

### **Elimination Rounds (28–29 July)**
#### **First Round (28 July)**
- **China Taipei 213** – **Denmark 195**
- **Russia 209** – **India 198**
- **Mexico 210** – **Ukraine 199**
- **Great Britain 208** – **Italy 200**

#### **Quarterfinals (29 July)**
- **South Korea 221** – **China Taipei 199**
- **United States 220** – **Russia 206**
- **China 208** – **Mexico 204**
- **Japan 217** – **Great Britain 207**

#### **Semifinals (29 July)**
- **South Korea 221** – **United States 206**
- **China 220** – **Japan 208**

#### **Bronze Medal Match (29 July)**
- **Japan 209** – **United States 207**

#### **Gold Medal Match (29 July)**
- **South Korea 210** – **China 191**

---

### **Final Standings & Medalists**
| **Medal** | **Team**       | **Archers**                     |
|-----------|----------------|---------------------------------|
| **Gold**  | South Korea    | Ki Bo-bae, Lee Sung-jin, Choi Hyeon-ju |
| **Silver**| China          | Cheng Ming, Fang Yuting, Xu Jing |
| **Bronze**| Japan          | Kaori Kawanaka, Ren Hayakawa, Miki Kanie |

---

### **Notable Facts**
1. **South Korea’s Dominance:**
   - This was South Korea’s **7th consecutive gold in women’s team archery** (1988–2012).
   - Ki Bo-bae (who also won individual gold) was part of the team.
   - South Korea set an Olympic record in the ranking round (1993 points).

2. **China’s Silver:**
   - China had won gold in **2008 (Beijing)**, but South Korea reclaimed the title.
   - Fang Yuting was the youngest member (18 years old).

3. **Japan’s Bronze:**
   - Their first Olympic medal in women’s team archery since **1988 (silver)**.

4. **United States’ Near-Podium:**
   - Lost to Japan by just **2 points** in the bronze match.
   - Khatuna Lorig (a 5-time Olympian) was the most experienced archer.

5. **Deepika Kumari’s Struggle:**
   - India’s star archer, ranked **#1 in the world** at the time, underperformed in the team event (India lost to Russia in the first round).

6. **Venue:**
   - Lord’s Cricket Ground was temporarily transformed into an archery range, with stands for 6,500 spectators.

---

### **Rules & Scoring**
- **Set System:** Matches were divided into **4 sets of 6 arrows (2 per archer per set)**.
  - The team with the higher score in a set earned **2 set points**; a tie gave **1 point each**.
  - First to **5 set points** won the match.
- **Arrow Values:**
  - Gold (10/9 points), Red (8/7), Blue (6/5), Black (4/3), White (2/1), Miss (0).

---

### **Legacy**
- South Korea’s victory extended their **unbeaten streak in women’s team archery** at the Olympics (they would go on to win again in **2016 and 2020**).
- The 2012 Olympics marked the **last time archery was held at Lord’s Cricket Ground** (the 2016 and 2020 editions used different venues).
